calls.reply:
I'm scoring these from what I remember of the mouse protein data set, not from the data itself. The classes combine genotype (control vs. trisomic), stimulation context (CS vs. SC), and drug treatment (memantine vs. saline).

Proteins that I recall as most discriminative in the original study and in later analyses: DYRK1A, ITSN1, pERK, BRAF, APP, SOD1 (overexpressed in trisomy), pCAMKII, pPKCG, CaNA, Ubiquitin, H3MeK4, AcetylH3K9, S6, pS6, SYP, pCFOS, ARC, Tau, GFAP, nNOS, and others. Learning-related markers such as pCFOS, SOD1, and BDNF also matter. Good features for separating the stimulation and drug effects include pPKCG, CaNA, and pCFOS. Frequently selected ones also include NR2A, pNR2A, pELK, Bcatenin, and AcetylH3K9.

The scores below follow this recollection.

calls.reply:
This is the mouse protein expression (Cortical Nuclear) dataset from Higuera et al. The classes combine genotype (control vs. trisomy), context-shock vs. shock-context stimulation, and memantine vs. saline treatment. From what I recall of the literature, the proteins that discriminate best include DYRK1A, ITSN1, pERK, BRAF, SOD1, APP, pELK, AcetylH3K9, CaNA, pCASP9, Ubiquitin, H3MeK4, and the others scored below. These scores come from that recall, not from the data.

Scores for the proteins I recall as most discriminative:
- Highest: ITSN1, pPKCAB, SOD1, APP, DYRK1A, BRAF, pELK, pCASP9, and Ubiquitin.
- Next: AcetylH3K9, H3MeK4, CaNA, pNR2A, NR2A, and the rest of the strong 0.6–0.7 group listed below.
- Remaining features get mid-range or low scores by the same recollection.
